questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of an algorithm in daily life?

expected_answer.value: A recipe listing the steps to make tea

options: A recipe listing the steps to make tea
A photograph of a cup of tea
The name of a tea brand

questions.prompt: An algorithm is written before a program is coded. Its main purpose is to:

expected_answer.value: plan the solution steps clearly

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a plan of the solution steps, written before coding so the logic is clear.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows the order in which a problem is usually solved with a computer?

expected_answer.value: Understand problem, write algorithm, code, test

options: Understand problem, write algorithm, code, test
Code, test, write algorithm, understand problem

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a suitable way to express an algorithm?

expected_answer.value: A video game console

questions.prompt: Which property says that every step of an algorithm must be clear and unambiguous?

questions.prompt: An algorithm that never stops after starting violates which property?

expected_answer.value: Finiteness

questions.prompt: Which statement about the output of an algorithm is true?

expected_answer.value: It should produce at least one result

options: It must always be a number
It should produce at least one result
It is optional and can be absent
It must be printed on paper
questions.explanation: A useful algorithm produces at least one output, which need not be numeric or printed.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a step-by-step procedure written in an English-like form, not tied to a programming language?

expected_answer.value: Pseudocode

questions.explanation: Pseudocode uses plain, structured wording to describe an algorithm without strict syntax.

questions.prompt: Which instruction is NOT acceptable inside an algorithm because it is ambiguous?

expected_answer.value: Add a suitable amount of sugar

options: Add a suitable amount of sugar
questions.explanation: 'A suitable amount' has no exact meaning, so it breaks the definiteness property.

options: Read A, B; print A + B
Read A, B; if A > B print A, else print B
